thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: A plug-and-play machine-monitoring system using non-invasive electrical-current clamps, an IoT gateway, optional operator tablet and SaaS dashboards to measure utilisation, downtime, productivity and energy. The company states that customers need the outcome addressed by its described product; precise quantified pain was not independently verified. Public evidence supports responsibility for hardware; supports only partial/shared responsibility for models/policies; does not establish responsibility for robot body, end effectors/tooling, simulation/training, integration, commissioning/qualification, remote operations, ongoing support/maintenance and hardware financing/RaaS. Overall integration responsibility is classified as customer_led. Commercial evidence: 3_partner_confirmed_or_customer_pilot; technical evidence: 4_named_partner_confirmed. These are public-evidence classifications, not proof of contract scope, uptime, economics or performance.
relevanceToIntegration: Indirect comparator: public evidence places physical integration or workflow adoption with the customer; product ownership is not evidence of hands-on customer-site integration.
evidenceGaps: Independent customer confirmation; exact integration/commissioning boundary; repeatability; pricing; deployment economics; current legal status where no registry source is cited.
